title: Nagata principal-open criterion for a property of primes
statement:
Let $S$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $P$ be a predicate on its ideals. Assume (i) whenever $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ are prime ideals and $P(\mathfrak p)$ holds, then $P(\mathfrak q)$ holds; and (ii) for each prime $\mathfrak p$ satisfying $P(\mathfrak p)$ there exists $g
otin\mathfrak p$ such that $P(\mathfrak q)$ holds for every prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq\mathfrak p$ with $g
otin\mathfrak q$. Then for each prime $\mathfrak p$ satisfying $P(\mathfrak p)$ there exists $h
otin\mathfrak p$ such that $P(\mathfrak q)$ holds for every prime $\mathfrak q$ with $h
otin\mathfrak q$.

lean.statement:
theorem Ideal.exists_notMem_forall_of_isNoetherianRing {S : Type*} [CommRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] (U : Ideal S → Prop)
    (hgen : ∀ P Q : Ideal S, P.IsPrime → Q.IsPrime → Q ≤ P → U P → U Q)
    (hloc : ∀ P : Ideal S, P.IsPrime → U P →
      ∃ g ∉ P, ∀ Q : Ideal S, Q.IsPrime → P ≤ Q → g ∉ Q → U Q)
    (P : Ideal S) [P.IsPrime] (hP : U P) :
    ∃ g ∉ P, ∀ Q : Ideal S, Q.IsPrime → g ∉ Q → U Q
lean.note: The source declaration is exactly Nagata’s principal-open criterion (Stacks Tag 0541): it uses a predicate U on ideals of a commutative Noetherian ring, generalization stability hgen, the local principal-neighborhood hypothesis hloc, and concludes a principal neighborhood D(g) on which U holds. The theorem’s explicit prime-ideal typeclass [P.IsPrime] and all quantified clauses match the node statement.
